Roberto De Zerbi post-match interview - Leeds v Spurs
It was somewhat surprising to see Roberto de Zerbi take a more peaceful approach when he faced the media at Elland Road after Tottenham's 1-0 defeat by Leeds United on Saturday afternoon.

The Spurs manager had been expected to come out swinging in the direction of the officials after his side's first Premier League loss since September, with much of the focus falling on referee John Brooks' decision not to send Jayden Bogle off for a late challenge on Mathys Tel during the first half.
It was a decision that no doubt impacted the game - and perhaps Tottenham's chances of earning a fourth consecutive Premier League victory for the first time since October 2023.
When Bogle caught Tel with his studs, the game was still goalless and Tottenham were arguably the team on top at Elland Road.
Following a lengthy video assistant referee (VAR) check that lasted more than four minutes, no further action was taken against the Leeds defender and the game resumed.
That was not the case for Frenchman Tel, who was unable to continue after sustaining a bruising injury to his left foot.
Former Premier League assistant referee Darren McCann said Bogle was "fortunate" not to be dismissed.
"Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent," McCann told BBC Sport. "He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch."
By the time play resumed, there was less than nine minutes of the first half remaining and Tottenham's momentum - and composure - were fading quickly.
De Zerbi's side never appeared to recover from the incident and, after the break, were outrun, outworked and outplayed by the home side.
Nevertheless, De Zerbi - perhaps buoyed by his side's recent rise up the table - refused to pinpoint Spurs' failings on the referee's decision.
"We deserved to lose the game in the second half and didn't play like we can," he told TNT Sports. "It's a journey for us because we can learn from this game.
"I am sorry for the performance in the second half - we didn't play like a top team. We didn't have the right character and physicality in the second half."

When the PA system at Elland Road confirmed there was a VAR check in progress, it seemed only a matter of time before Bogle would be shown a red card.

The Leeds defender was full-blooded in his pursuit of the ball from Tel and seemed certain to follow in the footsteps of Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta, who was sent off for a similar challenge against Spurs last weekend.
